title: Chapter 1: The Childhood Friends Who Became Idols and the Transfer Student Who Brings a Storm 3
content: Sayama and Ijuuin both chimed in at the same time. It seemed they were not satisfied with my explanation.

"Well, even so. I became an idol to make Kazukun's life easier, so I want to hear any request he makes. I don't mind at all; in fact, I want to support him. If I could, I'd give him all my money, and I hope he becomes so dependent on me that he can't live without me."
"Setsuna-sama!?"
"What are you saying, Takanashi-san! If you do that, he'll become not just a loser but a parasitic piece of trash! That's just pathetic! That's not okay, as a person!!"
"That's a harsh thing to say."
I couldn't help but retort at my friend's harsh words, but no one was listening to me. Everyone was focused on Setsuna.
However, the important thing is that Setsuna seemed to be focused on me, smiling as she looked at me.

"Yeah, being a parasite is fine. I promised to take care of Kazukun for life. If Kazukun is a hopeless loser, then he can't rely on anyone but me, and that's the best. He'll never leave my side, and I can take care of him without anyone interrupting me. There's no greater happiness than that. Right, Kazukun? You're happy to be taken care of by me, right? It must be true; you definitely don't want to work, right?"
"Yeah, that's right. Just make my life easy for me and take care of me, okay? If it ever comes to a point where I have to work, I won't accept it, even if you're my Childhood Friend."
"Hehe. I know that. I'll be the only one to take care of Kazukun..."
I felt like Setsuna's eyes were gradually clouding over, but it was probably just my imagination.
As long as she was willing to take care of me, I had no complaints.
With a sponsor on board, I was sure she would earn even more from now on. The "Hyaahhoi" future was just around the corner.
Just then, I heard a voice.
"...This is unacceptable."
"This is unacceptable! To leech off Setsuna-sama and suck her dry...! Even if heaven allows it, I will not permit it!!"
The one who shouted was Ijuuin.
She glared at me as if she would never acknowledge it, but to be honest, I was troubled by what she said.
"Even if you say that..."
"I will absolutely not allow it! Prepare yourself! I, Ijuuin Reika, will protect Setsuna-sama and Dimension Stars! at all costs!!!!"
With that, Ijuuin dashed out of the classroom.
I didn't even have the time to comment on the teacher's "Buh?!", which echoed as she opened the door, as her retreat was so dramatic.
The classmates left in the classroom, including me, were left speechless.
"...What was that about?"
"Who knows...?"
Faced with the storm that had passed, Setsuna and I could only tilt our heads in confusion.
"Yawn..."
The next morning, as I climbed the stairs to the classroom, I stifled a yawn.
"I really stayed up too late playing games. I'm so sleepy."
I rubbed my eyes, but there was no sign of the sleepiness fading away.
After updating the site and pulling gacha until around three in the morning, it was only natural.

Yesterday, after being asked various questions by my classmates, I ended up coming home late, and since there was a stream from my favorite Vtuber I found the other day, I prioritized that, which delayed my gaming session.
"That V, she really knows how to lift my spirits, so I can't help but get involved."

She had just started recently and had few viewers, a so-called bottom-tier Vtuber, but when I showed up during her stream, she would immediately get excited, and when I sent her tips, she'd shout, "Woohoo!!! God!!! Thank you for the blessings from above for a loser like me!!! Thank you so much, God!!!" in a loud, messy voice, which I highly appreciated.
It's not easy for a person to throw away their pride like that.
Even though her voice was rough, being fawned over like that made her seem almost like a pet, which was endearing.

Every time I was praised like that, I reaffirmed that I was a super winner in life, generous and compassionate enough to give money to others, even though I was a loser who couldn't become a true winner. It really lifted my spirits.
Well, it's just a little stress relief.
Throwing money at a bottom-tier Vtuber allows me to feel a sense of superiority while they get the money, creating a win-win relationship; it's one of my many hobbies.
"Oh, right, I promised to do a quest today. I can't just go to sleep now. I messed up."

I also had an online game as one of my hobbies, but the person I usually teamed up with had been busy lately and hadn't logged in much, but finally, they had some free time, so they invited me to play together again.

Since they've been helping me for a while, I couldn't just ditch the promise. They seemed to be going through a lot, so I prepared some items that would help in the quest, and I'm sure they'd be happy to receive them as a gift.
"That said, I'm still so sleepy..."
I thought maybe I should have just skipped school, but at this point, there was no way I could go back, so I trudged forward with a dazed gait.
I wanted to just lay my head down on my desk, and finally, when I arrived in front of the classroom, I lifted my heavy arms and opened the classroom door with a creak.
"Good morning—"
"You were late, Kazu-ma."
I tried to greet, but before I could finish, someone interrupted me.
"Huh? That's not how you respond. What a foolish reply, stupid Kazu-ma."
A direct hit of a harsh insult came out of nowhere. I almost retorted, but my instincts stopped me.
That voice was familiar. In fact, it was too familiar.
Moreover, when I caught sight of the silver-blonde hair, neatly trimmed at the shoulders, I couldn't help but murmur her name.
"Arisa, huh."
"Hmph, I'm glad you remembered. Get your act together, sleepyhead."
Just by calling her name, I was met with her usual sharp tongue.
This behavior of hers had not changed since childhood.
There was no doubt about it. The beautiful girl with silver hair in front of me was my other Childhood Friend, Tsukishiro Arisa.

Her face was perfectly doll-like, and her figure was outstanding. Her haughty attitude was a reflection of her confidence, and in reality, her hidden potential and specs were likely on par with Setsuna.
Of course, someone like her couldn't be an ordinary person; she was now one half of the double ace alongside Setsuna, standing shoulder to shoulder in Damenz.
Competitive and strong-willed, she possessed exceptional abilities that shone brightly on stage. That was the girl I knew as Arisa.
But for some reason, my proud Childhood Friend was looking at me with a bewildered expression.
I hadn't done anything to upset her, so I raised my right hand lightly to greet her again.
"Anyway, good morning. Has it been since Friday? It's been a while since we met."
"Yeah, yeah, good morning. Yes, it has. You still look as lazy as ever."
"There's a deep reason for that. By the way, aren't you working today... yawn."
I stifled a big yawn that slipped out.
Even though I was starting to wake up a bit from the usual banter with Arisa, it seemed I still hadn't fully awakened.
"You have no credibility yawning while saying that. You stayed up late again, didn't you? I always tell you not to live carelessly just because your parents aren't home."
"Yeah, that's true. But I can't help it..."
As the sleepiness hit me again, the stronger-willed Childhood Friend approached me, making a clattering sound.
"Come on, get it together."
"Ugh."
Then she slapped my cheeks with both hands.
It wasn't hard enough to hurt, but it seemed to have woken me up a bit, shaking off some of the sleepiness.
"Look into my eyes. Now take a deep breath. Okay, do it."
With no energy to resist, I followed her instructions and took a deep breath.
It seemed to be surprisingly effective, as I noticed my head starting to work after repeating the breaths while looking into Arisa's blue eyes.
"Are you okay now?"
"Yeah, I think I'm fine now. Thanks, Arisa."
"Yeah... Wait, you have bedhead. Seriously, if I'm not around, you just let yourself go."
Now she was acting like a mother, stretching up to pat my head.
While gazing at my Childhood Friend's beautiful face so close, I couldn't help but mutter to myself.
(She's still as caring as ever, and a bit defenseless too.)
It seemed Arisa, unlike Setsuna, lacked a certain awareness of her idol status.
She still actively tried to take care of me, but the distance was just too close.
While it was certainly helpful for me, this was a classroom with people around.
The morning classroom is usually noisy, but right now it was oddly quiet, and it was clear that if I shifted my gaze, everyone was looking at us.
Yesterday, with Ijuuin's appearance, even when Setsuna came, everyone had been in a buoyant mood, but now that the Transfer Student was gone,
Especially the boys were staring at us... or rather, me, with jealous eyes.
"I'm going to kill him... Why is that loser with Tsukishiro-san...?" "I'm a big fan of Arisa-chan in Damenz... this is NTR... it hurts... but why? It's strangely pleasant...!"
Yeah, that's scary. I genuinely felt a sense of danger.
It felt like there was even a murderous intent in my classmates' eyes, which couldn't be just my imagination.
There were some weird comments, but I decided to ignore them.
"Hey, your tie is crooked too. You really are a handful. Setsuna just lets you get away with everything, so I have to be the one to keep you in line..."
"Arisa, weren't you supposed to be working today?"
I looked down at Arisa, who had started fixing my tie, and asked about what I had almost said earlier.
I had heard in advance that Arisa was taking the day off for work yesterday, but I realized I hadn't asked about today's schedule.
While it's true that Dimension Stars! has been gaining popularity, Damenz is actually a unit where each member has a high level of attention.
Since they are composed of beautiful girls with different directions, it's one of their strengths that they can take on a wide range of jobs.
Because of that, it's common for them to have separate jobs come up lately.
The fact that Arisa was here while Setsuna wasn't might mean that Setsuna had a job today and couldn't come.
As I was thinking about that, Arisa looked up at me with interest, but then she quickly returned her gaze to my tie, speaking again.
"I'm off today. By the way, Setsuna has a job, so she won't be here today. It's a shame that the Childhood Friends aren't together."
"Oh, I see."
It seemed my guess was correct.
However, I wasn't too concerned about that, so I let it slide.
Well, I did have some business with her, so I was a bit disappointed.
(I spent too much yesterday on gacha and super chats, so I was hoping to get some extra money from her... but I guess it can't be helped.)
Since she was earning money for me, I couldn't complain.
I wasn't the kind of person to ask her to take a day off to give me money.
So I intended to end the conversation there, but it seemed Arisa had other ideas.
Perhaps my casual response displeased her, as she furrowed her brows and shot me a sharp glare.
"...What? Are you dissatisfied with me?"
"Just answer me. Can't you listen to what I'm saying?"
I was at a loss. I was weak against that gaze.
I didn't care much when my parents scolded me, but I've always had a hard time when Arisa got angry.
She usually doesn't say anything wrong, and I can tell she cares about me.
It feels wrong to go against her, and I end up obeying her.
And this time was no exception.
"Ugh... Fine. I'll tell you, so don't look at me like that."
Resigned, I decided to confess as she had asked, but the content wasn't anything significant.
"Well, that's fine."

"That said, my spending is pretty normal. I mainly use it for gacha in mobile games and throwing super chats at Vtubers. After that, I buy games and PC parts, but that's within a reasonable range for a high school student."
"...That's normal, I guess. But how much money are you spending?"
Cat asked with a puzzled expression.
Well, at this point, it was the same, and it wasn't something I needed to hide, so I decided to answer honestly.
"Huh? All of it."
"Eh?"

"I mean, all of it. Before I knew it, it was gone. If I don't fully upgrade the characters or weapons I pull in gacha, it doesn't feel satisfying, and when I throw super chats, they often disappear before I know it. If the PC requires higher specs, it never ends, and when I replace the graphics card, the money just flies away."
The more money I spend, the more it disappears, but that's just how it is.
Hobbies are like that.
If you're doing something you love, it would be counterproductive to build up stress, and that's my philosophy.

"I also occasionally stay at a fancy hotel if I have leftover money, or I eat delicious food. I went to a sushi place that doesn't have a conveyor belt recently, and it was pretty good. In the future, I want to try renting a place for a cosplay bunny café for a day."

"Oh, speaking of bunnies, yesterday, two mobile games I've been into, Bunny Bakaile and Usamusu Pretty Bunny, both had gacha updates at the same time. They both had popular characters that are considered must-haves, so I fully upgraded them. Especially Bunny Bakaile, which is known as 'Bunny Baka' because it only has bunny characters in gacha! As a bunny girl lover, I had no choice but to roll for it. You get what I mean, right?"
"No, I don't get it. The idiot is Kuzuha-kun. You're way past your spending limit, and what you're doing is just plain stupid."
"What are you saying?"
To call someone an idiot to their face is quite rude.
I'm not buying luxury cars or partying with girls; I'm spending my money in a pretty healthy way for a typical high school boy.
"You're not using your money wisely. You're spending it all as soon as you get it, and I bet you're not saving at all."

"Actually, that's true. Yesterday, after I uploaded a gacha video online, I played the new game I bought until around three in the morning, but my favorite Vtuber was streaming. While playing the game, I casually threw some super chats, and before I knew it, I spent quite a bit. My wallet is feeling light now. I wish the streamers would think more about their viewers; it really gets to me."
"That's not the point. You're just a loser. What you're doing is just pathetic. You're worse than a parasite."
"You're being way too harsh on me."
I was indignant at Cat's harsh words.
I'm a saint for giving money to a lesser-known Vtuber.
There's no reason for me to be called a loser; in fact, I should be praised for it.
"Well, that's why I'm out of money. I'm so broke I can't buy anything at the school store."
"Haa... You're really hopeless."
After hearing my explanation, Arisa sighed.
I thought I was being pretty straightforward, but it seemed she was exasperated.
"With that attitude, you were planning to ask Setsuna for money, weren't you?"
"Oh, you figured it out?"
"I know. How many years have we been friends? Stupid Kazuha."
It seemed that the earlier exchanges had built up Arisa's frustration.
She looked at me as if to say, "What are you doing?"
"Kazuha, that's not okay. The adults were lamenting that they raised you wrong. Just because Setsuna is a good girl doesn't mean you can take her money and waste it. You should reflect on that!"
